Tim Cook is just weeks away from stepping down as Apple CEO, with John Ternus set to officially take over the reins on September 1. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan believes Ternus has the potential to usher in a bolder, higher-risk new era for Apple.

Ternus is expected to be more willing to take risks on new products, acquisitions, and research and development after becoming CEO

The handover of the Apple CEO role is nearly complete. So far, the company has worked hard to emphasise the continuity Ternus will bring to the position.

But not everyone on Wall Street is convinced Ternus will hew so closely to Cook's playbook.

In a research note seen by The Street, Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan reiterated a strong "Buy" rating on Apple. A key part of that rating is the expectation that Ternus will extend Cook's legacy while also having a greater "risk appetite." Mo Faruk writes:

The bank highlighted that Apple's abandonment of its cash-neutral net target is an early signal that management may be more willing to deploy capital. This will translate into higher R&D spending, more capex, and potentially larger acquisitions—all categories that weren't defining features of Cook-era strategy. BofA thinks Apple under Ternus could move faster into entirely new categories, including AI glasses, AirPods with cameras, a smart ring, smart home, personal assistant, and robotics.

Ultimately, BofA believes Ternus will extend Cook's legacy of turning Apple into an extremely profitable global enterprise, but also expects him to lean on the company's strong position to make bolder moves going forward.

When Ternus first takes over as CEO, we're unlikely to see any major changes. But over the coming months, any potential differences in priorities may gradually come to light.

What are your expectations for John Ternus as Apple CEO? Let us know in the comments.
